title: Merge Three Sorted Arrays Without Duplicates
statement:
You are given three integer arrays `a`, `b` and `c`, each sorted in **non-decreasing** order. An array may contain repeated values.

Merge them into one array that is sorted in **strictly increasing** order and contains every distinct value that appears in at least one of the three arrays exactly once.

The interviewer's expectation is that you use the fact that the inputs are already sorted (a three-pointer merge) rather than concatenating and sorting everything.

**Follow-up:** generalise to `k` sorted arrays and discuss how a min-heap changes the complexity.
inputFormat: Three lines, one per array. Each line starts with the length of the array, followed by its elements: `len v1 v2 ... v_len`.
outputFormat: Print the merged distinct values in increasing order, separated by single spaces.
constraints: each array is sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: The value 4 occurs in all three arrays but is printed once. Every other value is unique.
Duplicates inside one array and across arrays collapse into a single copy each: the distinct values are 1, 2 and 3.
Negative numbers are handled the same way; -5 appears in two arrays and -7 twice in one.

hints: Keep one pointer per array, like the merge step of merge sort, but with three pointers.
At each step take the smallest of the three current values and advance every pointer that currently points at that value.
Only append the value when it differs from the last value you appended; that also removes duplicates inside a single array.
